entities.name: Red tattoo hypersensitivity
observations: Delayed inflammatory reactions in red tattoo areas include lichenoid, eczematous, and pseudolymphomatous presentations.

entities.name: Azo tattoo pigments
observations: Azo pigments including Pigment Red 22, 170, and 210 are repeatedly identified in chronic allergic tattoo reactions; direct causal attribution can be limited by ink mixtures and negative tests.

entities.name: Quinacridone pigments
observations: A small clinical case series reported delayed tattoo reactions involving quinacridones Violet 19 and Red 122; purified-pigment sensitization was not established in the available report.

entities.name: PMID:31626330
observations: Chemical analysis of 104 chronic allergic tattoo reaction biopsies frequently identified azo pigments Pigment Red 22, 210, and 170; some samples lacked detectable red pigment, and metals were also found.

entities.name: PMID:25441375
observations: Six-patient series described seven tattoo reactions, including five involving azo pigments and two involving quinacridones; patch/prick testing was largely uninformative.

entities.name: PMID:25040844
observations: In 90 patients with chronic tattoo reactions, common-allergen and culprit-ink patch tests were negative; in-skin hapten formation was proposed as an explanation.
